title: Connexions projectives et uniformisation : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: X/S is a relative (smooth) scheme. P is an augmented O_X-algebra that is separated and complete for the J-adic topology, where J is the augmentation ideal. Ω denotes J/J^2. The next page shows that the intended case is P = O of the formal completion P̂ of a P^1-bundle along a section σ, the bundle being associated to an extension 0→Ω→E→O→0. So Ω is invertible, and P is a 'formal disc bundle' over X.

Definition. A 'connexion d'algèbre' on P is an additive map C : P → P ⊗̂ Ω^1_{X/S} satisfying:
- Leibniz: C(fg) = f C(g) + g C(f);
- normalisation: C(λ·1) = 1 ⊗ dλ for λ ∈ O_X.
The marginal remark appears to say that C is NOT required to preserve the augmentation. This matters: the section σ need not be horizontal.

Local description. Over an affine, choose an augmentation-compatible isomorphism P ≅ Sym^(Ω), the completed symmetric algebra (this implicitly needs gr P ≅ Sym Ω). By Leibniz and continuity, C is determined by its restriction to Ω. That restriction is an additive map
 Ω → ∏_{i≥0} Sym^i(Ω) ⊗ Ω^1_{X/S},
with components ω_i. The dλ term only enters degree 1, so:
- ω_i is O_X-linear for i ≠ 1, i.e. ω_i ∈ Γ(Ω^{-1} ⊗ Ω^{⊗i} ⊗ Ω^1) = Γ(Ω^{⊗(i-1)} ⊗ Ω^1_{X/S}) when Ω has rank 1;
- ω_1 is an ordinary module connection on Ω.
This is the formal-coordinate expansion of a connection on a formal disc bundle.

Graded part. Because of the ω_0 term, C lowers the filtration by one: C(J^i) ⊂ J^{i-1} ⊗̂ Ω^1. Hence C induces maps
 gr^i P = Ω^i → gr^{i-1} ⊗ Ω^1 = Ω^{i-1} ⊗ Ω^1_{X/S}.
These are O_X-linear and form the derivation of Sym(Ω) induced by ω_0 : Ω → Ω^1_{X/S}. In particular ω_0 is intrinsic, independent of the chosen splitting.

What it serves (continued on the next page):
- C is called 'regular' when ω_0 : Ω → Ω^1_{X/S} is an isomorphism. This is the Kodaira–Spencer/transversality condition of the section, i.e. the indigenous-bundle / oper condition.
- Regular connections, modulo augmented automorphisms of Sym^(Ω) that are the identity mod m^3, are compared with projective connections on P^1-bundles with section.
- Using the group-theoretic lemma of the previous page (G_0 × C_0 ≅ C, giving G(c) ≅ G/G_0), this yields the classical torsor structure under quadratic differentials Γ(X, Ω^{⊗2}).

Overall: a formal-geometric framework for projective structures and uniformisation ('connexions projectives et uniformisation').
errors: The local isomorphism P ≅ Sym^(Ω) needs the unstated hypothesis gr_J P ≅ Sym(J/J^2) (formally smooth augmented algebra); completeness and separatedness alone do not suffice.

The induced graded map is a derivation of Sym(Ω), sending x^i to i·x^{i-1}⊗ω_0(x). It is not Sym^i-linear as the text seems to say, and the written formula C̃(ω_i)=ω_i⊗ω_0 omits the factor i. This matters in positive or mixed characteristic over S, where regularity on higher graded pieces fails for i ≡ 0 mod p.
The identification of ω_i with Γ(Ω^{⊗(i-1)}⊗Ω^1) silently assumes Ω invertible (rank 1). That holds in the intended P^1-bundle case but not for general augmented P.
'O_S-linear' is weaker than what holds: the graded map is O_X-linear, since the dλ term dies in the graded quotient.

ideas.what: Projective connection encoded as a Leibniz connection on the complete augmented algebra of the formal completion of a P^1-bundle along a section, not necessarily respecting the augmentation
ideas.modern_name: Flat connection on a formal disc bundle / Gelfand–Kazhdan formal geometry description of projective structures (Aut O-torsor reductions)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gelfand–Kazhdan (1971) for formal geometry; Ben-Zvi–Frenkel (c. 2000–2004) for projective structures/opers via formal coordinates

ideas.what: Expansion of C|Ω into components ω_i: ω_0 linear, ω_1 a module connection, ω_i (i≥2) tensors in Ω^{⊗(i-1)}⊗Ω^1
ideas.modern_name: Taylor/jet expansion of a connection on a formal neighbourhood

ideas.what: Intrinsic degree −1 graded symbol ω_0 : Ω → Ω^1_{X/S}; 'regular' iff ω_0 is an isomorphism
ideas.modern_name: Kodaira–Spencer map of the section / oper (indigenous bundle) transversality condition

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates projective structures on curves over an arbitrary base S as 'regular' algebra connections on the completed symmetric algebra of the formal completion of a P^1-bundle along a section. The regularity is an intrinsic symbol condition (ω_0 invertible), and the moduli of such connections is controlled by automorphisms of the formal disc trivial mod m^3. This anticipates the formal-coordinate (Aut O) approach to projective structures and opers of Ben-Zvi–Frenkel, and the relative/arithmetic indigenous bundles of Mochizuki.
missed.quote: C : P → P ⊗̂ Ω^1_{X/S} connexion d'algèbre ... C(J^i) ⊂ J^{i-1} ⊗̂ Ω^1_{X/S}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is an early, purely algebraic, characteristic-free formal-disc framework for uniformisation and opers over a general base S. Historically it shows Grothendieck's work on projective connections and uniformisation predating the oper literature. The degree-lowering symbol ω_0 also makes visible the characteristic-p obstruction (factor i) relevant to dormant opers.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is the standard theory of projective structures and indigenous bundles, but written in an unusual formal-disc / completed-algebra language over a general base, with a clean intrinsic regularity criterion. This resembles later formal-geometry treatments of opers. It is a notable unpublished framing rather than a new theorem.
transcription_corrections: Final formula likely reads C̃(ω^i) = (i)ω^{i-1}⊗ϖ_0 or similar, with ϖ_0 (varpi) as on the next page, rather than C̃(ω_i)=ω_i⊗ω_0; the components are probably written ϖ_i throughout.
'Ω^{⊗(i-1)}' in the interpretation of ϖ_i should be understood as Ω^{-1}⊗Ω^{⊗i} for invertible Ω.

The marginal note after 'connexion d'algèbre' probably says the connection is not assumed compatible with the augmentation ('non nécessairement compatible à l'augmentation'), not '(une dérivation ... pour une d'augmentation)'.
'qui est O_S-linéaire, et = Sym(Ω)-linéaire' likely contains 'O_X-linéaire' or is the start of a derivation statement.
